findings: Both captures explain an eligible payment method authorization as a hold that reserves funds. The Charge card capture_before field is the specific authorization expiry. Successful manual authorization leaves the Intent requires_capture, emits payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated when the customer completes the manual-capture payment process, and allows inspection of amount_capturable. Capture uses a PaymentIntent ID, including for Checkout, and defaults to the authorized amount. If an entirely uncaptured authorization expires, release and canceled follow, and merchant cancellation uses the PaymentIntent (old 8-12, 166-194, new 9-13, 135-159).

The merchant can initiate manual authorization in Dashboard or by setting Checkout Session payment_intent_data.capture_method or the PaymentIntent’s capture_method. Method-level capture_method on card lets only cards take a hold while other eligible payment methods can still be used with their own behavior. After attaching card details/confirming the PaymentIntent, verify authorization rather than inferring from Checkout creation, method selection or a successful API request (old 62-77, 101-166, new 62-77, 91-135).

The dated standard online Visa CIT is 7 days and MIT is listed as five days, exact 4 days 18 hours. Visa in-person is also exact 4 days 18 hours. Other listed brands' online windows are seven days and Mastercard/AmEx/Discover card-present windows two days. CIT/MIT classification depends on participation signals rather than off_session alone. Both captures reserve eligible extended authorization and online-card overcapture/multicapture qualifications. Per-method hold windows and initial Affirm/Afterpay down-payment/installment treatment remain method-specific (old 18-60, 172-190, new 19-60, 141-155).

Maintain the existing Checkout and prior raw routes. Payment Intents concept lines 127-131 hold separate versioned request-field evidence. These standalone guide examples do not themselves identify the required API version.

November's auth_expiry default captures before expiry (about six hours early fallback); end_of_day uses UTC; target_delay takes days or hours and both can be combined up to 30 total days. If the hold expires sooner than the specified delay, Stripe prioritizes capture before authorization expiry. Both dates allow manual capture/cancel before automatic capture. The new early-access form requests follow-up only (old 196-243, new 161-213).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-place-a-hold-on-a-payment-method-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-auth-and-capture-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-auth-and-capture.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/place-a-hold-on-a-payment-method`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/place-a-hold-on-a-payment-method, both captures describe merchant authorization of an eligible payment method to hold funds, followed by capture before the Charge’s capture_before deadline. Successful manual authorization leaves the PaymentIntent requires_capture. The customer completion flow emits payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated, and you can inspect amount_capturable. An entirely uncaptured expiry releases the funds and changes status to canceled. Dashboard and Checkout Session payment_intent_data manual paths remain, while the direct PaymentIntent permits method-level manual capture for cards in a mixed-method flow. Capture the PaymentIntent, not the Session, with the full amount by default. Ordinary partial capture releases the remainder, with eligible multicapture governed separately. The hold guide links canceling an authorization via its PaymentIntent. The separate November 7 Cancel API limits direct cancellation of a Checkout Session-linked Intent to requires_capture and directs other cases to Session expiration (old raw lines 192-194, new raw lines 157-159 and separate Cancel API lines 5-11). Both hold guides say Affirm may require a down payment for very large orders. If it does, it collects it at authorization and refunds it if the payment is not captured, with 30 days to capture the remaining balance (old raw lines 54-57, new raw lines 53-57). November also describes the private-preview card automatic_delayed capture before expiry, with capture_by timing and earlier hold expiry taking precedence. source-stripe-auth-and-capture.md covers the central flow but still has April’s timing control and overstates PayPal’s extension from ten to twenty days as automatic rather than an attempt subject to the settlement preference qualification, while omitting the expiry locator and capture-ready event (old raw lines 8-60, old raw lines 101-194 and old raw lines 196-243, compared with new raw lines 9-60, new raw lines 91-159 and new raw lines 161-213).
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/place-a-hold-on-a-payment-method, update source-stripe-auth-and-capture.md with November's private-preview capture_by modes auth_expiry by default, end_of_day in UTC and target_delay using a capture_delay hash of days/hours, which may combine to no more than 30 days. Preserve April’s capture_delay_days example as dated. Both captures override an overlong delay to capture before the authorization expires, describe an approximately six-hour backup and allow prior manual capture or cancellation. The early-access form only requests contact (old raw lines 196-243, new raw lines 161-213). November replaces payment_method_types with allowed_payment_method_types in the explicit mixed-method example, while the per-method option stays the same (old raw lines 118-158, new raw lines 104-127). For Japan-based accounts, the up-to-30-day JPY treatment for Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Diners Club and Discover stays, but November points non-JPY/AmEx to the applicable standard windows instead of the April seven-day wording. Preserve the dated Visa history and unchanged exact table durations (old raw lines 18-46, new raw lines 19-45). cURL and changed link targets otherwise illustrate or navigate. Retain the original raw, the reciprocal Payment Intents concept link and the Checkout concept route.
